records.real_world_identity_notes: Porsche 911 GT3 Cup built by Porsche Motorsport for its one-make Carrera Cup and Supercup championships, running a 3.8-litre flat six of 460 hp through a six-speed dog-type gearbox shifted by paddles.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is stated by a registered source.
records.identity_basis: A registered source establishes the car, its engine and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
records.specification_basis: The source states a six-speed dog-type gearbox operated by paddles, and the live drive selected six paddle gears with automatic cut and blip and a clutch needed to pull away.
records.confidence_notes: Guided testing directly established the gear count, the standing-start clutch, the clutchless running shifts, and the automatic cut and blip state.
control_notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies neither, and the clutch is needed to pull away.

The gearbox is dog-type, which is stated by the registered source rather than inferred. A dog box would ordinarily want a rev-matched downshift, but this car blips its own, so the driver is not asked for one.
The registered source notes this was the first Porsche brand trophy car shifted by paddles rather than a lever, which matches the paddle actuation the drive observed.
The two Cup cars share a gearbox specification and were driven separately; nothing is inherited between them.
records.driver_summary: Porsche dog-type gearbox, but the car blips its own downshifts, so there is no rev-matching to do. The clutch is needed only to pull away.
